source: 23 frozen outcome-blind final deal audits, then manifest labels
interpretation: Deal-level observed patterns, not proved causes of WON/LOST or estimates of predictive lift.

patterns.name: Material technical fit or proof still unresolved at visible endpoint
patterns.definition: A customer-relevant fit, sample test, or integration answer remains a concrete next-step dependency in the retained view.
patterns.process_change_to_test: Before a firm proposal, document the customer's critical product/line constraints and agree a test or explicit acceptance path for the highest-risk fit question.
patterns.limits: An open technical question also appears in WON; outcome labels do not prove that resolving it changes conversion.

patterns.name: Customer-reported budget or project-priority deferral
patterns.definition: The customer directly describes funding, another project, or an organizational pause as constraining the next purchase step.
patterns.process_change_to_test: Record the decision owner, funding checkpoint, and agreed revisit date; offer a scoped or staged alternative only when the buyer confirms it is useful.
patterns.limits: Customer statements about funding and external conditions are not independently verified; WON cases also had funding dependencies.

patterns.name: Direct customer comparison with another offer or supplier
patterns.definition: A customer-sourced event explicitly mentions evaluating another supplier, test, or competing proposal.
patterns.process_change_to_test: Ask which comparable requirements and proof points decide the choice; respond with a short side-by-side fit and validation plan.
patterns.limits: Comparison itself is buying activity and occurs in a WON case; it is not a negative signal on its own.

patterns.name: Material scope or review-information rework after first proposal
patterns.definition: The visible proposal path requires a substantive specification revision or missing technical/review information before the buyer can decide.
patterns.process_change_to_test: Use a short pre-proposal checklist for line interface, representative formats, must-have functions, acceptance proof, and buyer review documents.
patterns.limits: Substantial rework also occurs in WON; some changes originated with customers after the first proposal.

patterns.name: Customer explicitly objects to follow-up frequency
patterns.definition: A customer directly says calls or payment reminders are too frequent or inconvenient.
patterns.process_change_to_test: Agree the next contact date and channel with the buyer, and route payment checks through the agreed accounting contact where available.
patterns.limits: The same friction appears in a WON deal; no causal effect on these outcomes is established.
